<reason>A made the decisive comparison: mandatory relative closeness can sacrifice wheelchair users’ coverage or affordability, whereas enforceable accessibility and maximum-wait standards can prioritize usable journeys. B persuasively established the harm of unequal waits but did not establish why parity should prevail in the constrained-budget case. A answered the pressure questions candidly; B’s proposal to share reductions acknowledged opportunity costs that its closing subsequently denied. B also repeatedly caricatured A’s substantive alternative as merely providing ramps.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s strongest response was that sharing coverage cuts does not restore a lost journey. B then described an evening service inaccessible to wheelchairs, failing to answer A’s actual example: sacrificing an already-accessible evening route to improve pickup parity elsewhere.</best_rebuttal>
